passage: Saturday: when Aunty and Uncle visited, Jatin wailed loudly for a chocolate. "Oh, give him one," said Aunty, and Ramesh handed it over. Sunday: at dinner Jatin folded his arms. "Then I will not eat." Ramesh smiled and stayed calm. "Dinner is here when you are ready." Jatin ate after a while. The next Saturday, the guests came again and Jatin began to cry loudly, but Ramesh only said, "Not today." Jatin peeked at the guests, hiccuped, then went to play.

qa.q: What did Jatin ask for when Aunty and Uncle visited?
qa.a: He wailed loudly for a chocolate.

qa.q: Why did Jatin keep crying loudly in front of visitors?
qa.a: It worked the first time, because the guests said give him one and Ramesh handed it over. So he learned that pressure could win.

qa.q: What did Ramesh change that made the crying stop working?
qa.a: He stayed kind and steady, said dinner was there when Jatin was ready, and said "Not today" when the guests came, so shouting no longer won.

qa.q: How might Aunty and Uncle feel on the second Saturday when Jatin cries?
qa.a: They may feel awkward or want to help, but seeing Ramesh stay calm shows them the limit is the parents' decision, which can spare Jatin the pressure to keep crying.

grounding: The child says he will not eat or cries loudly in front of visitors so they say yes; steady parents stop rewarding pressure.

passage: The power cut plunged the flat into darkness and the baby began to wail. Bhupen, five, picked up the torch, walked to the cot and patted his baby brother's tummy. "Shh, shh." It did not help, so he ran with the torch to the kitchen. "Mummy, he is crying!" Alka hurried in. "Thank you, Bhupen, you helped so much." She lifted the baby. Then she said, "Now go and finish your puzzle. Looking after him is my job." 🙂

qa.q: What did Bhupen carry to the cot?
qa.a: He picked up the torch.

qa.q: How might Bhupen feel when Alka says "you helped so much"?
qa.a: He feels big and needed. He patted the baby and fetched Mummy on his own.

qa.q: Why did Alka tell Bhupen to go and finish his puzzle?
qa.a: She thanked him but did not make him a permanent little parent, because he is a child too. 😊

qa.q: What might the baby have needed that Bhupen could not give?
qa.a: The baby may need feeding or holding, which only Alka can do. Bhupen did what he could and got Mummy.

grounding: My baby brother cries and I pat him and fetch Mummy; I feel big and needed, and the parent thanks me without making me a little parent.

passage: Every evening when Preeti got home, Jagdish had his blocks ready to show her. Today the baby started crying just as Jagdish was placing the top block, and Preeti ran to the cot. Jagdish stood there, holding the block. Nobody looked at his tower. He swept it over with his arm and the blocks clattered across the floor. Preeti turned. "Oh, Jagdish. You want me too, don't you?" She handed him the baby's wipes. "Please pass me those." Later she sat with him alone to rebuild the tower.

qa.q: What did Jagdish sweep over with his arm?
qa.a: He swept his tower over with his arm.

qa.q: Why did Jagdish knock down the tower?
qa.a: He felt forgotten because his mother ran to the baby, and knocking it over was a way to be noticed.

qa.q: What did Preeti do that helps Jagdish feel seen?
qa.a: She said aloud that he wanted her too, gave him a small job passing the wipes, and later sat with him alone to rebuild the tower.

qa.q: How might Preeti feel when the tower crashes while she is soothing the baby?
qa.a: She is probably stretched between two children and tired. Her gentle words show she understands why he did it.

grounding: When the baby cries my parent runs to him and I feel forgotten and act out; a small job and time together help me feel seen.

passage: The baby was crying again and the sound filled the flat. Rania pressed both hands over her ears and scrunched her face. Make it stop, she thought. Jin's wails bounced off the walls. She felt a hot, prickly feeling in her chest, and for a second her hand hovered near his blanket. Instead she stepped back, walked to her room and pulled out her jigsaw. She sat on the rug, put on a song in her head and started to look for edge pieces.

qa.q: What did Rania press over her ears?
qa.a: She pressed both hands over her ears.

qa.q: What was Rania feeling as she pressed her hands over her ears?
qa.a: She was annoyed and wanted the noise to stop, and she felt a prickly, hot feeling in her chest. That feeling is normal.

qa.q: What did Rania do that was a wise choice?
qa.a: She stepped back, walked to her room and played with her jigsaw, instead of doing anything to the baby.

qa.q: How might Jin's crying look from an adult's view when Rania walks away?
qa.a: The adult sees a baby who needs help and a big sister who found her own way through, and could thank her. They may not know how hard the noise was for her.

grounding: The crying is loud and I cover my ears and want it to stop; I walk away and play elsewhere.

passage: Note from Lalit, class teacher. Chaitanya's baby brother came home last week. At circle time Chaitanya scowled and said, "Everyone brings presents for the baby. Send him back." I did not tell him off. I said, "It is hard when everybody visits the baby," and made him helper of the day. His father told me at pick-up that Chaitanya hit the baby's hand and was gently, firmly stopped and told hands are not for hitting. His routine at home has stayed the same.

qa.q: Who came home last week?
qa.a: Chaitanya's baby brother came home last week.

qa.q: What was Chaitanya feeling when he said "Send him back"?
qa.a: He felt invisible and angry, because everyone was visiting and bringing presents for the baby.

qa.q: What did the adults do that helps Chaitanya?
qa.a: Lalit accepted the feeling and gave him a job, and at home his routine was kept and his hitting was stopped gently and firmly. 🤍

qa.q: How might Chaitanya's father have felt telling Lalit about the hit?
qa.a: He may have been worried and a little embarrassed, but he wanted help. Telling the teacher lets home and school treat Chaitanya the same way.

grounding: Everyone visits the baby and I feel invisible and angry and say send him back; wise adults accept the feeling, keep my routine and include me.

passage: Deepak tiptoed to the cot in the bedroom and touched the tiny fingers of his baby sister Mahima. They curled around his thumb. He held his breath. "Her nails are so small," he whispered, amazed and tender. "Can I bring her a diaper, Mummy?" He carefully fetched one from the shelf. Later, when Mummy fed Mahima and did not look up, Deepak sat down hard and frowned. "You are always with her," he muttered. Then he crept back to peek at the tiny hand.

qa.q: What did Mahima's fingers curl around?
qa.a: They curled around his thumb.

qa.q: What was Deepak feeling when he whispered about her tiny nails?
qa.a: He felt amazed and tender towards his new sister. His held breath and wish to fetch a diaper show it.

qa.q: What can a parent do when Deepak feels both love and jealousy in one day?
qa.a: She can accept both feelings as true and keep including him, for example by letting him bring things. 😊

qa.q: How might Mummy see Deepak when he frowns while she feeds Mahima?
qa.a: She may see a child who loves the baby but also misses her attention. That can help her make time for him too.

grounding: I stroke the baby's tiny hand and feel amazed and tender and want to help; love and jealousy can be true on the same day.

passage:
"Mumma, Jaggu wants the baby bottle," said Jagdish in a squeaky voice.
"You are five, Jagdish." Preeti rubbed her eyes, the baby fussing on her shoulder. Then she stopped. "Sorry. I am tired, and it is not your fault."
"Am I a baby too?"
"You are my big boy and I love you." She kissed his hair. "When she sleeps, it will be you and me, no phone. What shall we do?"
He thought. "Cards!"
"Cards it is."

qa.q: What did Jagdish ask for in a squeaky voice?
qa.a: He said Jaggu wants the baby bottle.

qa.q: Why did Jagdish talk like a baby?
qa.a: He feels pushed out while Mummy is busy with the baby, and baby talk is a way of getting close to her again.

qa.q: What did Preeti do to reassure him?
qa.a: She admitted she was tired and said it was not his fault, told him he is her big boy, and promised time for just the two of them when the baby sleeps.

qa.q: How might Preeti be feeling as she holds the fussing baby and talks to Jagdish?
qa.a: She is tired and stretched, and probably a little guilty about snapping. Her apology and her promise show she wants to be there for both children.

grounding: Mummy is tired and busy with the baby and I feel pushed out and use baby talk; one-to-one attention helps.

passage: Relatives were arriving, the doorbell kept ringing and the baby was crying in the next room. Nirmala hurried to feed the baby, and Tenzin stood by the shoe rack holding his toy truck. "Is there space for me?" he asked in a small voice. Nirmala stopped and pulled him close. "You are still my big boy and my little boy, and my lap has room for you both." Tenzin's shoulders relaxed and he climbed up beside the baby. "I can hold her foot," he said. 😊

qa.q: What was Tenzin holding by the shoe rack?
qa.a: He was holding his toy truck.

qa.q: What was Tenzin worried about when he asked "Is there space for me?"
qa.a: He worried that the baby had taken his place and there was no room left for him in his mother's care.

qa.q: How did Nirmala's words help Tenzin, even though she was rushing?
qa.a: She stopped and said he is still her big boy and little boy and that her lap has room for both. That told him his place was safe. 😊

qa.q: How might Tenzin's view of the baby change after his mother's reassurance?
qa.a: He may now feel proud to be an elder brother, as his offer to hold the baby's foot suggests, rather than jealous.

grounding: My parent says I am still her big and little one and there is room for both; I feel secure and the jealousy softens into pride.

passage: Note from Yash, for Rashmi's mother while she rests. Dadi arrived this afternoon with a bag of sweets and a rattle. She walked past the crib, crouched down and hugged Rashmi first. "You are my special one," she said. Rashmi's face lit up and she leaned right into her shoulder. Only then did Dadi go and look at the baby. Later Rashmi carried the rattle to the crib herself and showed it to her. I think this helped her feel safe.

qa.q: What did Dadi bring with her?
qa.a: She brought a bag of sweets and a rattle.

qa.q: How was Rashmi feeling when she leaned into Dadi's shoulder?
qa.a: She felt safe and important again. Her face lighting up shows that being hugged first meant a lot.

qa.q: What did Dadi do that protects an older child during a new-baby time?
qa.a: She noticed Rashmi first, hugged her and told her she is special before looking at the baby, so Rashmi did not feel replaced.

qa.q: How might Rashmi's mother feel when she reads Yash's note?
qa.a: She is probably relieved and grateful, since she is tired and busy with the baby and can see that Rashmi is being noticed.

grounding: Dadi hugs me first, not the baby, and says I am her special one; I feel safe and important again.

passage: Anders came back from the toilet to find his rocket drawing torn in two. Emil stood beside it, chewing his sleeve. Heat rushed through Anders's whole body and he punched Emil's arm. Emil yelled and hit back, and both boys were crying when Mamma came in. "Hands are not for hitting. Tell Emil with words." Anders gulped. "You tore my rocket and I am so mad!" "I did not mean to," Emil sniffed. Mamma fetched the tape while both boys sat glaring, a bit red-eyed.

qa.q: What did Anders find torn in two?
qa.a: He found his rocket drawing torn in two.

qa.q: What was Anders feeling when he punched Emil's arm?
qa.a: He was furious. The anger rushed through his whole body and he lashed out before words came.

qa.q: What worked better than hitting once Mamma came in?
qa.a: Saying with words, "You tore my rocket and I am so mad," got a hearing, and Mamma fetched tape to fix it. Hitting only made Emil angry and he hit back.

qa.q: How might Emil see the torn drawing and Anders's punch?
qa.a: Emil says he did not mean to, so he may feel guilty and hurt at being hit. He hit back because he was scared and upset too.

grounding: My sibling broke my drawing and I hit back; a wise child says you broke it, I am mad, and gets help.
